name: Enchey Monastery

local_name.name: Enchey
local_name.meaning: Usually translated as 'solitary', so Enchey Gompa is 'the solitary monastery'

tagline: Gangtok's Nyingma monastery on the ridge, 3 km above MG Marg
meta_description: Enchey Monastery, Gangtok: a 1909 Nyingma gompa on an 1840s hermitage site, its January–February Chaam, prayer times, taxi fares and how to visit with respect.
summary: Enchey Monastery is a Nyingma gompa on a pine-covered ridge about 3 km north-east of MG Marg, at roughly 1,860 m. A small monastery stood here from the 1840s; the present building dates from 1909. Visit in the early morning for prayers, or in January–February for its Detor Chaam mask dance. No permit needed.
intro: Enchey is the monastery Gangtok people mean when they say 'the gompa up the hill'. It stands on a ridge above the town on the road towards Nathu La, about 3 km and 15 minutes by taxi from MG Marg, among tall conifers and lines of prayer flags. Wikipedia records that a small monastery was first built here in the 1840s, at the place where the tantric master Lama Druptob Karpo had his hermitage, and that the present building, with its golden cupola and pagoda-like roof, was put up in 1909.

It belongs to the Nyingma school, the oldest Tibetan Buddhist tradition and the one most closely tied to Sikkim's royal history; like other Nyingma monasteries in the state, it falls under Pemayangtse in West Sikkim. Inside the two-storey prayer hall the walls are covered with murals of guardian kings and deities, the four pillars are carved and painted, and the monastery keeps a large collection of masks for its annual dances.

Most visitors give Enchey 30–45 minutes on a Gangtok sightseeing round. Come at about 7–8 am instead, when the monks chant in the hall and the town is still quiet below. In January or February, on the 18th and 19th days of the 12th Tibetan month, the courtyard fills for the Detor Chaam. Dates follow the lunar calendar, so check current status before you travel.

story.title: The lama who flew from Maenam Hill
story.text: Gangtok was only a small hamlet when Enchey's story begins. According to the tradition recorded in Wikipedia's article on the monastery, the site was blessed by Lama Druptob Karpo, an adept of tantric practice remembered for his power of flight, who is said to have flown here from Maenam Hill in South Sikkim and set up a small hermitage on the ridge. A monastery was first built at the spot in the 1840s, and the hamlet below became a place of pilgrimage. The tradition also holds that Guru Padmasambhava subdued the local spirits here, so the protector deities of Kangchenjunga and Yabdean are believed to reside in the monastery, which is why many Gangtok households still come to Enchey with their wishes and worries. The building you see today was raised in 1909. It was badly damaged by fire in 1947 and rebuilt in 1948 with help from devotees, and it was cracked again by earthquakes in 1980, 1988 and 2006. Each time it has been repaired. Treat the flying lama as what it is, a sacred tradition, and the dates as history.

little_known.fact: Enchey was badly damaged by fire in 1947 and rebuilt the following year with the support of devotees, according to Wikipedia's history of the monastery.
A survey after the 14 February 2006 earthquake, a moderate 5.7 quake, found wide cracks in Enchey's 500 mm stone walls; earlier quakes in 1980 and 1988 had also damaged it.
Besides the yearly Detor Chaam, Enchey performs a Singhe Chaam, the snow-lion dance, once every three years or so, and marks Pang Lhabsol in late summer.

facts: Visit from Gangtok, 45 minutes to 1 hour
Nyingma monastery, Detor Chaam, morning prayers

highlights.title: Morning prayers in the hall
highlights.text: From about 7 am the monks gather to chant, with drums, cymbals and long horns. Sit quietly at the back, shoes off, and you hear Enchey as a working monastery rather than a stop on a taxi tour. Afternoon prayers are shorter and less predictable; ask at the door.

highlights.title: The Detor Chaam
highlights.text: On the 18th and 19th days of the 12th Tibetan month, usually January or February, monks in masks and brocade dance the defeat of obstacles before the new year. Gangtok families climb the hill to watch. Arrive by 9 am for a place on the courtyard steps.

highlights.title: Murals and carved pillars
highlights.text: The prayer hall walls carry paintings of the four guardian kings and many Buddhist deities, and the four main pillars are carved and painted. Statues of the Buddha and Guru Padmasambhava face the entrance. Photography inside is usually not allowed, so look slowly instead.

highlights.title: The ridge and the conifers
highlights.text: The approach road runs through an avenue of tall conifers past the TV tower, and the monastery terrace looks over the town. On clear mornings from October to March the Kangchenjunga range is visible from near the monastery. It is the calmest corner of central Gangtok.

highlights.title: A short walk to Ganesh Tok
highlights.text: Enchey sits on the same ridge road, NH310, as Ganesh Tok and the Himalayan Zoological Park. With a taxi you can link all three in two hours; fit walkers can do the uphill stretch on foot along the road in about 40–50 minutes, watching for traffic.

how_to_reach.text: A reserved local taxi from MG Marg or Lal Bazaar to Enchey costs about ₹200–300 one way, more if the driver waits. Most drivers include Enchey in the half-day 'points' tour with Ganesh Tok, Tashi View Point and the Do Drul Chorten for about ₹1,500–2,500 a car.

From MG Marg it is about 3 km and a steady climb of roughly 200 m via the road past the Secretariat side of town; allow 50–60 minutes up and 35 minutes down. Pavements are patchy, so walk in daylight and keep to the side of the road.

Enchey is inside Gangtok, about 125 km and 4.5–5 hours by car from Bagdogra (IXB) or NJP on NH10. NH10 closes after monsoon slides; the alternative is via Kalimpong or Algarah. Visit on your first full day in town, and check current status before you travel.

where_to_stay: Enchey is ten to fifteen minutes from any central Gangtok hotel, so stay wherever suits your budget. The upper town around Enchey and Chandmari has small family-run guesthouses with quiet nights and valley views, and is handy for dawn visits to Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok. On a budget, Mintokling Guest House and Hotel Sonam Delek near MG Marg are reliable. For value, Netuk House and Hotel Tibet are close to the Do Drul Chorten road. For a splurge, Elgin Nor-Khill and Mayfair are a short drive away.
tips: Arrive between 7 and 8 am to hear the morning chanting before the taxi tours arrive.
Walk clockwise around the hall and prayer wheels, and remove shoes before entering.
Do not photograph inside the prayer hall unless a monk clearly says you may.
For the Chaam, carry a cushion or mat for the stone steps and a warm layer for January mornings.
Combine Enchey with Ganesh Tok and the Do Drul Chorten in one short taxi round.

experiences.title: Morning prayers at Enchey
experiences.summary: Reach Enchey before the sightseeing taxis and sit at the back of the prayer hall while the monks chant with drums and horns. An hour that shows Gangtok's oldest monastic site as a working religious house, not a photo stop.
body: Take a taxi up from MG Marg at about 6:45 am, or walk if you are already acclimatised. The town is quiet at this hour, the ridge smells of pine and woodsmoke, and you are likely to share the courtyard only with a few local people turning the prayer wheels. Walk once round the building clockwise before going in, which is what the regular visitors do.

Leave your shoes at the door and sit on the floor or a bench at the back. Prayers may last most of an hour, with chanting led by a senior monk, the deep note of the long horns and the clash of cymbals at set points. Young monks serve butter tea to the assembly. Do not walk between the monks and the altar, and keep your phone silent and in your pocket.

When the prayers end, take time with the murals: the four guardian kings by the entrance and the deities on the side walls. If a monk is free and willing, a short question about the Nyingma school or the coming Chaam is usually welcome. Leave a small offering in the donation box if you wish.

faqs.q: What time are morning prayers at Enchey Monastery?
faqs.a: Morning prayers usually begin around 7 am and can run close to an hour, but times shift with the ritual calendar and the season. We suggest arriving by 7 am and asking at the door. On festival days the timetable changes entirely, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can tourists sit inside during prayers at Enchey?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if you are quiet and respectful. Remove shoes, sit at the back, keep feet pointing away from the altar and do not photograph without clear permission. If a monk indicates that the hall is closed for a ritual, wait outside; there is plenty to see in the courtyard.

faqs.q: How do we get to Enchey early in the morning?
faqs.a: Ask your hotel to book a local taxi the evening before; a one-way ride from MG Marg costs about ₹200–300. Fit walkers can climb the 3 km in about 50–60 minutes. Shared taxis are scarce before 8 am, so do not rely on them for an early start.

experiences.title: Watching the Detor Chaam at Enchey
experiences.best_time: 18th–19th days of the 12th Tibetan month, January or February
experiences.summary: Each winter Enchey's monks perform the Detor Chaam, two days of masked dances in the courtyard before the Tibetan new year. Gangtok families come in their best clothes; visitors are welcome to watch from the edges.
body: Chaam is a ritual dance of Tibetan Buddhism, performed by monks to destroy obstacles and negative forces before the new year. At Enchey it falls on the 18th and 19th days of the 12th month of the Tibetan calendar, which usually means January or February. The dancers wear brocade robes and painted masks of protector deities, including Mahakala, and move slowly to drums, cymbals and long horns. Jesters slip in between the solemn dances and make the crowd laugh.

Arrive by 9 am to find a place on the steps or along the courtyard wall. The dances go on with breaks through the day, and the second day usually builds to the main ritual. Bring water, a snack, a cushion and a warm layer, since winter mornings at 1,860 m start cold even in sunshine.

Stay behind the rope or the line the monks indicate, never step into the dance ground, and avoid flash. Local families bring children and elders and often sit in the same place each year, so be ready to squeeze up. Dates move with the lunar calendar every year; we confirm them in December, and you should check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the Enchey Monastery Chaam in 2027?
faqs.a: The Detor Chaam falls on the 18th and 19th days of the 12th Tibetan month, which usually lands in January or February. The exact Gregorian dates change every year with the lunar calendar and are announced locally. We confirm them each December; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can we photograph the Chaam at Enchey?
faqs.a: Photography of the dances in the open courtyard is generally tolerated, but use no flash, stay behind the rope and never step into the dance ground for a better angle. Some moments of the ritual may be off limits; follow instructions from the monks and volunteers at once.

faqs.q: Is the Enchey Chaam crowded?
faqs.a: It draws a large local crowd, especially on the second day and at weekends, but it is far smaller than big-city festivals. Arrive by 9 am for a step to sit on. Families with small children should pick a spot near the exit, and seniors should bring a folding stool or cushion.

experiences.title: Ridge walk from Enchey to Ganesh Tok
experiences.image_query: Gangtok ridge road prayer flags pine
experiences.summary: Walk the upper ridge road from Enchey to Ganesh Tok, past the TV tower and through conifers, with views over the town and, on clear mornings, the Kangchenjunga range. Easy to moderate, about 2 km uphill, with a taxi back down.
body: After the morning prayers at Enchey, set off up the ridge on the road towards Ganesh Tok. It is a public road, NH310, so walk on the side and watch for army trucks and taxis, but traffic is light early in the day. The road climbs gently through an avenue of conifers and passes the TV tower, with gaps in the trees looking over the roofs of Gangtok and across the valley to Rumtek.

The distance is about 2 km with a climb of roughly 120 m, which takes most people 40–50 minutes at an easy pace. At about 1,900–2,000 m you will breathe a little harder than at home, so stop often. On clear days between October and March, the Kangchenjunga range shows to the north-west.

At Ganesh Tok, climb the short flight of steps to the shrine and the viewing terrace, then cross to the Himalayan Zoological Park if you have time for the red pandas. A taxi back to MG Marg costs about ₹250–350. We do not suggest this walk after dark or in heavy monsoon rain.

faqs.q: Is it safe to walk from Enchey to Ganesh Tok?
faqs.a: Yes, in daylight, if you keep to the side of the road. It is a public highway used by army vehicles and taxis, with patchy pavement. Walk single file on bends, wear bright clothing in mist, and avoid the walk after dark or in heavy rain, when visibility drops quickly.

faqs.q: How long is the walk from Enchey to Ganesh Tok?
faqs.a: About 2 km with a gentle climb of roughly 120 m. Most people take 40–50 minutes with photo stops. The return is easiest by taxi, about ₹250–350 to MG Marg, or you can walk downhill in around 35 minutes.

faqs.q: Can children and seniors do the Enchey to Ganesh Tok walk?
faqs.a: Older children usually manage it well. Seniors who walk regularly at home can do it slowly, but the traffic and lack of pavement make it less relaxing than it sounds. For families with small children or less steady walkers, take a taxi between the two and walk the short paths at each site.

experiences.title: Dawn light at Enchey for photographers
experiences.summary: At sunrise the golden cupola, prayer flags and pine trunks of Enchey catch low light, and the ridge is almost empty. A quiet photography session for early risers, with clear rules on what not to shoot.
body: Enchey faces the morning across the ridge, and between October and March the first sun lights the cupola and the upper prayer flags while the courtyard is still in shade. Arrive 20 minutes before sunrise. A standard zoom is enough; a short telephoto helps for details of the carved and painted windows and for the mountains on clear days.

The best frames are outside: the facade with its strings of flags, monks crossing the courtyard with butter lamps, and the line of conifers along the approach road. Shoot from the edges and never block the path of people coming to pray. A tripod is fine outside if you keep it out of the way.

Do not photograph inside the prayer hall without explicit permission, and ask before taking portraits of monks or lay visitors; a polite gesture and a nod is enough. When the light goes flat around 8:30 am, head down for breakfast or carry on to Ganesh Tok. Winter mornings are cold, so bring gloves that let you work the camera.

faqs.q: What time is sunrise in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Roughly 4:50–5:10 am in May and June and about 6:15–6:25 am in December and January, with October and March in between. The ridge hides the sun for a few minutes longer. Check a sunrise app for your date and arrive 20 minutes earlier.

faqs.q: Can I fly a drone at Enchey Monastery?
faqs.a: We advise against it. Gangtok's upper ridge lies close to army areas and government installations, and drone flying in Sikkim needs permission from the authorities. Flying over a working monastery is also disrespectful. Check current status before you travel, and leave the drone at the hotel unless you have written permission.

faqs.q: Is Kangchenjunga visible from Enchey?
faqs.a: On clear mornings, mostly from October to March, the Kangchenjunga range is visible from the ridge near the monastery. Trees block parts of the view, so Ganesh Tok, Hanuman Tok and Tashi View Point give wider panoramas. From April to September cloud usually hides the peaks by mid-morning.

faqs.q: How far is Enchey Monastery from MG Marg?
faqs.a: About 3 km by road, 10–15 minutes in a taxi, on the ridge north-east of the market towards the Nathu La road. A one-way taxi costs about ₹200–300. Walkers should allow 50–60 minutes uphill. It is often included in Gangtok's half-day sightseeing tours with Ganesh Tok and Tashi View Point.

faqs.q: When was Enchey Monastery built?
faqs.a: A small monastery was first built on the site in the 1840s, where Lama Druptob Karpo had his hermitage. The present building dates from 1909. It was damaged by fire in 1947 and rebuilt in 1948, and repaired after earthquakes in 1980, 1988 and 2006, according to Wikipedia.

faqs.q: Which school of Buddhism does Enchey follow?
faqs.a: Enchey belongs to the Nyingma school, the oldest of the Tibetan Buddhist traditions, which traces itself to Guru Padmasambhava. Like other Nyingma monasteries in Sikkim, it falls under the authority of Pemayangtse Monastery in West Sikkim. Rumtek and Lingdum, across the valley, belong to the Kagyu school.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee at Enchey Monastery?
faqs.a: No ticket is usually charged. A small offering in the donation box is welcome but never required. Remove shoes before entering the hall, cover shoulders and knees, and do not photograph inside without permission. Rules can change, so follow any notices at the gate.

faqs.q: When is the Enchey Chaam?
faqs.a: The annual Detor Chaam is held on the 18th and 19th days of the 12th month of the Tibetan calendar, usually in January or February. Dates change each year with the lunar calendar. A larger snow-lion dance is performed every few years. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What are Enchey Monastery's opening hours?
faqs.a: There are no formal posted hours, but the courtyard is generally open from early morning to late afternoon, and the hall opens for prayers in the morning. Visit between 7 am and 4 pm for the best chance of finding it open. On ritual days some areas may be closed.

faqs.q: How much time do we need at Enchey?
faqs.a: Thirty to forty-five minutes covers the courtyard, the hall and the murals. Allow an hour if you want to sit through part of the morning prayers, and a half day for the Chaam. Combine it with Ganesh Tok and the Do Drul Chorten for a two-to-three-hour morning.

faqs.q: Is Enchey Monastery suitable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxis stop close to the gate, and the courtyard is reached by a short slope and a few steps. The hall floor is level. At about 1,860 m, seniors should walk slowly and rest. On Chaam days the crowd and stone steps make it more tiring, so bring a cushion or stool.

faqs.q: Can we visit Enchey and Rumtek on the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. Visit Enchey early, then cross the valley via Ranipool to Rumtek, about 24 km and an hour from Gangtok, adding Lingdum near Ranka on the way. A reserved small car for the round costs about ₹3,500–4,500 for the day in 2026. Check current rates before you travel.
